failure_mode: "In a working shelf it returns the cradle instead of the target, and it does it confidently. Divers have gone home certain of a shape that was four metres of singing steel."

The hand sonar exists because ax_brine_dark leaves nothing else. Light stops at four metres
and the vault is eleven metres long, so anything a diver wants to know about the far end has
to be touched or pinged, and touching it means crossing.

The instrument is a fist-sized transducer on a lanyard, pressed to the jaw. It is crude on
purpose: the co-op buys the model with no display, because a display would need a lamp. What
comes back is range and bulk. A diver who has spent twenty years on the same four objects
can do a great deal more with that than the specification allows - she knows the cradle's
return, and she knows what the seal ring sounds like whole - but this is a trained ear
guessing well, not an instrument reporting. The register has refused twice to accept a sonar
return as evidence of condition.

And every use of it is a broadcast. There is no such thing as a quiet ping in a flooded room
eleven metres long. A diver who pings has told everyone in the water where she is, and, if
they know her, what she was worried about.
